tools.name: shinjuku_setup
tools.description: The wallet is not set up on this machine yet. Call this when the user wants to pay a paid URL, check a balance, or shield USDC. It asks the user to confirm in this client (with the spending caps, Tor, and the user's own wallet address, optional: later sends to it need no question), then creates a self-custody wallet on this machine (keys and a random passphrase in private local files; no tool takes or returns them), downloads and checks the setup files (about 191 MB, minutes), and switches this server to the wallet tools. Takes no arguments. Call it again with no arguments as `next` says for the stage (confirming, waiting: another setup of this wallet runs and this one waits for it, tor, platform, release, passphrase, wallet, proof-tools, program-check, config, done; declined, no_tor or failed: the setup ended, and this call answers why). A decline creates nothing (mcp_setup_declined). A client that cannot confirm is refused (mcp_setup_needs_terminal) with the terminal command; a client that declines at once without showing the dialog gets mcp_setup_declined with the same terminal command.

instructions: This Shinjuku Shield wallet is NOT SET UP yet: every money tool answers wallet_not_set_up. When the user wants to pay, check a balance, or add money, call shinjuku_setup: it asks the user to confirm, creates the wallet and downloads the setup files (minutes: call again as next says). At stage done the wallet tools work. After setup: A self-custody Shinjuku Shield wallet on this machine; no tool takes or returns its keys or passphrase. Each answer's say is one plain sentence for the user; other fields are data. Never tell the user a tool, field, code or protocol name (x402, MCP) unless told to. Map a plain request to one tool: "what is my balance" -> wallet_balance (safe any time); "add money" / "deposit" / "move USDC in from Phantom or an exchange" -> wallet_add_funds (a one-time address; the next wallet_balance after the USDC arrives makes it private); "shield the USDC on this wallet's own address" -> wallet_shield; "stop" / "cancel" -> wallet_cancel (the request_id of what to stop); "pay this URL" -> pay_for_service (no preview needed); "what does this URL cost" -> check_price (only when asked); "find a paid API for X" -> find_paid_services, then pay its url; "send 2 USDC to <address>" -> wallet_unshield; "show my payments" -> wallet_receipts; "sell, swap, or send a token other than USDC" -> no tool: this wallet does not do that, so say so and offer no sale; "which AI models" -> inference_models; "ask an AI model" -> inference_chat; "give my other AI app a private AI" -> inference_server. wallet_balance answers ONE balance (balanceAtomic); pay_for_service pays any paid URL from it. Fields ending in Atomic count 1000000 per USDC; tell the user USDC. The wallet does its own upkeep. A shield, add-funds or unshield call can run for minutes: call again with the SAME request_id as next says. Pass your own request_id to pay_for_service: the same one never pays or moves money twice (a code ending in _retry_same_request: call again with it). pay_for_service never pays above the spending limits (one payment; 24 hours); with none, only the balance bounds it. Never claim a payment happened unless the answer has a transaction. After a pay or send call that stopped, failed, or this app calls rejected or interrupted, call wallet_receipts (a payment) or wallet_cancel (a send; no request_id) before you say whether it happened; never say nothing moved without that. Privacy: the chain does not show which wallet paid, but this app and its model provider see every URL, body, price and answer you handle; reach a seller or its domain only through these tools, never yourself (no curl, browser, DNS or DNS-over-HTTPS lookup), also when the user asks for no Tor: that shows their IP address to the site or a DNS company. When a poolSwitch.items[] item has tellUser true, tell the user its message once, in plain words; the wallet moves the balance itself.
